title: OA legacy consumer aligner: map OpenAI Completions requests/responses to Redwood streaming + function-call structured outputs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: A number of legacy clients integrate with the OpenAI Chat Completions HTTP API and expect a single final JSON response (with optional streaming fallback). Redwood's runtime provides richer streaming deltas and a function-calling structured-output surface that can differ in event shape, ordering, and metadata. This ticket implements a purpose-built alignment layer that accepts incoming OpenAI-style Completions requests and reliably produces responses that preserve client expectations while enabling Redwood streaming and function-call semantics under the hood. Scope: - Translate incoming OpenAI-completions request fields (messages, temperature, top_p, max_tokens, user) into Redwood inference requests with preserved intent and token budgets. - Emit responses back in the shape legacy clients expect: support both non-streaming final JSON and a streaming SSE-compatible delta stream that mirrors the OpenAI stream protocol where feasible. - Map function calling: support both (A) clients that rely on the older single-call 'choices[].finish_reason' + serialized JSON payload and (B) clients that expect incremental function_call.name/arguments in stream deltas. - Ensure idempotency and deterministic reassembly for clients that perform retries. - Preserve provenance fields (model, model_version, request_id) and add telemetry tags without breaking parity checks. Non-goals: - Rewriting client-side SDKs. We only provide server-side compatibility layer and documentation for migration.
acceptance_criteria: Incoming OpenAI-completions request shape is accepted without 4xx when required fields are present (messages, model) and mapped to Redwood request targets.
Streaming path: server emits SSE events that legacy clients can consume and reassemble into the same final text/model output as a non-streaming call (where semantics permit).

Function calling mapping: for a function invocation produced by the model, both streaming consumers and non-streaming consumers receive an observable event or final payload consistent with OpenAI's documented behavior (name + arguments as JSON string).

Structured outputs: when a model provides JSON schema-guided structured output, the compatibility layer surfaces the structured payload in the legacy shape (choices[].message/content) and also emits Redwood structured metadata in separate telemetry headers, without altering content bytes expected by clients.
Edge cases: partial deltas, out-of-order deltas, and reconnect heuristics are handled so clients do not see corrupted JSON or duplicated content across retries.

Comprehensive test coverage: unit tests for transformation logic, integration tests against a simulated legacy client, and a load test demonstrating no >10% latency regression at target QPS compared to native Redwood endpoint.
implementation_notes: Design an explicit request translator function that produces: (1) normalized token budgets, (2) role/name mapping, (3) function-calling hints and allowed functions set.

Streaming: implement an emitter that renders SSE frames compatible with OpenAI framed stream semantics (data: {delta...}, data: [DONE]) while internally using Redwood delta events; use a small reconciliation buffer to coalesce immediate sub-deltas for deterministic ordering.

Function calls: maintain a compact state machine per-request to detect the earliest model action that constitutes a function call, then synthesize both a streaming function_call delta and a final choices[].finish_reason + message payload for non-streaming clients.

Idempotency keys: honor x-idempotency-key when present and persist mapping for 5 minutes to support retries. On conflict, return consistent final payload or the same stream token sequence to prevent double-execution of side-effects.
Telemetry: attach request tags (compat-layer:v1, legacy-client:true, mapped-model:<model>) and emit span logs for each mapping decision to aid debugging.

Backpressure: rate-limit translation work per-tenant to avoid added queuing; when necessary, degrade to synchronous non-streaming path with an explicit X-Redwood-Warning header documented in migration notes.
Docs: publish a migration guide with examples showing how a client can switch to native Redwood shapes while remaining compatible.
Rollout: feature-flag behind 'oa-legacy-aligner' with canary for 5% of traffic, then 25%, 50%, 100% gated by error rate and latency metrics.
testing_plan: Unit tests for request translation permutations: message roles, function list mismatch, absent 'user' field, temperature/top_p mappings.
Integration tests: spawn a simulated legacy client that consumes SSE and non-streaming responses; assert byte-equal reassembly for identical model seeds in the simulator.
Chaos tests: simulate reconnects mid-stream, duplicate events, and verify idempotency semantics for retries with the same idempotency key.
Load test: synthetic workload at expected production mix (30% streaming, 10% function-calls) validating p95 latency and error budget.
Security review: verify no PII leaks when serializing function arguments and add an audit log entry for each function invocation bridged by the layer.
